'''Esther Sans Takeuchi''' (born '''Esther Sans''', {{langx|lv|Estere Sāns}}) is a [[materials scientist]] and chemical engineer, working on [[energy storage]] systems and power sources for biomedical devices. She is also a distinguished professor at [[Stony Brook University]] and a chief scientist at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]. She holds more than 150 U.S. patents.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-adv.htm&r=0&p=1&f=S&l=50&Query=in%2FTakeuchi-Esther%24&d=PTXT |title=USPTO Patent Search for Esther Takeuchi |access-date=2014-11-18 |archive-date=2018-08-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180805233615/http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-adv.htm&r=0&p=1&f=S&l=50&Query=in%2FTakeuchi-Esther%24&d=PTXT |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://commcgi.cc.stonybrook.edu/am2/publish/General_University_News_2/Esther_Takeuchi_Selected_to_Receive_2013_E_V_Murphree_Award.shtml "Esther Takeuchi Selected to Receive 2013 E.V. Murphree Award"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130204014635/http://commcgi.cc.stonybrook.edu/am2/publish/General_University_News_2/Esther_Takeuchi_Selected_to_Receive_2013_E_V_Murphree_Award.shtml |date=2013-02-04 }}, SUNY Stony Brook, September 6, 2012.</ref> “The battery was invented once and reinvented over 100 times. I don’t own the patent. The company does. It was called Greatbatch. Now it’s called Integer Corp. When you join a company, you sign over your patent rights to the company.”<ref name="Executive Profile: Esther Takeuchi">{{cite web |last1=Solnik |first1=Claude |title=Executive Profile: Esther Takeuchi |url=https://libn.com/2018/07/16/executive-profile-esther-takeuchi/ |website=libn.com |date=16 July 2018 |publisher=Long Island Business News |access-date=3 April 2019}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Takeuchi is the daughter of Mary (''Marija'') and Rudolf Sans (''Rūdolfs Sāns)'', Second World War refugees from Latvia.<ref name="baltic">Jerry Zremski, [http://www.baltic-course.com/eng/education/?doc=19329 "Daughter of Latvian refugees receives top technological award at White House"], ''The Buffalo News'', Oct. 8, 2009, republished on ''The Baltic Course'', Oct. 14, 2009.</ref> Rudolf and Mary fled [[Soviet occupation of the Baltic States|Soviet-occupied]] Latvia for Germany in 1945, living in a refugee camp for several years, ultimately immigrating to the United States.<ref name="baltic" />

Takeuchi graduated from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1975 having majored in chemistry and history. She then worked on her Ph.D. in organic chemistry at the [[Ohio State University]] until 1981, under the direction of Dr. Harold Shechter. Her graduate research focused on the reactions of alkoxides with (chloromethyl)trisubstituted silanes.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Sans|first=Esther Alma|date=1981|title=Reactions of halomethyltrisubstitutedsilanes with alkoxides |url=https://etd.ohiolink.edu/pg_10?0::NO:10:P10_ETD_SUBID:135346 |degree= PhD |url-status=dead |publisher=Ohio State University|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181118000723/https://etd.ohiolink.edu/pg_10?0::NO:10:P10_ETD_SUBID:135346 | oclc=8798338 |archive-date=2018-11-18}}</ref>

While working on her Ph.D., she met Kenneth J. Takeuchi and the two married on May 15, 1982.<ref name=desmond2016/>

After completing post-doctoral training in electrochemistry at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] and the [[University of Buffalo]], she worked at Greatbatch Inc. in [[Clarence, New York]] for 22 years. It was here, under the funding of [[Wilson Greatbatch]], that Takeuchi continued development of the Li/SVO battery. She has also worked on batteries for neuro stimulators, drug delivery systems, pacemakers, and also industrial batteries for environments concerning high temperatures, vibrations, and need of reliability.<ref name="Executive Profile: Esther Takeuchi"/>

In 2007, she joined academia at the University of Buffalo as the Greatbatch Professor of Advanced Power Sources. She is currently a distinguished professor at Stony Brook University in the departments of chemistry, and material science and engineering. She was selected as the 2013 recipient of the E.V. Murphree Award in Industrial and Engineering Chemistry, sponsored by [[ExxonMobil|Exxon Mobil]].<ref name="bnl">{{cite web|url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=111450|title=Esther Takeuchi Selected to Receive 2013 E.V. Murphree Award|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=Brookhaven National Laboratory|access-date=19 September 2013}}</ref> Takeuchi is also a Fellow of [[The Electrochemical Society]] and served as the organization's president from 2011–2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=ECS President Esther S. Takeuchi|url=http://www.electrochem.org/dl/hc/presidents/takeuchi.htm|website=The Electrochemical Society}}</ref>

== Research projects ==
On July 16, 2018, Takeuchi’s company was awarded a $12 million grant from the US Department of Energy, to focus on the development of high energy and high power batteriesfor use in electric vehicles or in combination with renewable solar energy systems and renewable energy farms.<ref name="Executive Profile: Esther Takeuchi"/>
The company also has several projects funded by the DOE and supported by partners such as Mercedes-Benz.

== Vision ==
Takeuchi envisions creating an entity bringing together Stony Brook, Brookhaven National Lab, federal funding, state funding, industry, and philanthropy, creating an institute focused on energy and the environment.<ref name="Executive Profile: Esther Takeuchi"/>

== Recognition ==
Takeuchi has been primarily recognized and awarded for her innovation regarding implantable cardiac defibrillators.<ref>{{cite web |title=Esther Sans Takeuchi |url=https://www.nationalmedals.org/laureates/esther-sans-takeuchi |website=National Science Technology and Medals Foundation |access-date=3 April 2019}}</ref> The innovation is a new type of battery technology regarding a new cathode material, highly conductive electrolyte, and a cell design enabling high power and resulting in the creation of a silver vanadium oxide battery.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=Karen |title=Takeuchi Receives European Inventor Award 2018 in the Non-EPO Countries Category |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=112960 |website=Brookhaven National Laboratory |access-date=3 April 2019}}</ref> The batteries are powerful, miniature in size, and have a long life<ref>{{cite web |last1=Solnik |first1=Claude |title=Executive Profile:Esther Takeuchi |url=https://libn.com/2018/07/16/executive-profile-esther-takeuchi/ |website=libn.com |date=16 July 2018 |publisher=Long Island Business News |access-date=3 April 2019}}</ref>, characteristics that benefit ICDs and their ability to help people with irregular rhythms and beating frequencies within their hearts.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=Karen |title=Takeuchi Receives European Inventor Award 2018 in the Non-EPO Countries Category |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=112960 |website=Brookhaven National Laboratory |access-date=3 April 2019}}</ref> The SVO batteries can last for around five years, compared to the average life of around a year for the other forms of batteries. If traditional forms of batteries are used, patients with the implant have to go through surgery regularly to replace the devices and ensure the functionality of the implant, so the use of SVO batteries means that devices need to be replaced less frequently.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Burns |first1=Sarah |last2=Harrington |first2=John |title=32 Amazing Women Inventors |url=https://247wallst.com/special-report/2018/09/17/living-women-inventors-you-should-know-about-now/3/ |website=24/7 Wall St |date=17 September 2018 |access-date=3 April 2019}}</ref> Initially launched into the marketplace in the late 1980s and early 1990s, these SVO batteries are still prevalent and widely used today.

== Awards ==
* European Inventor Award in the "non-EPO countries" category, presented by the [[European Patent Office]] (EPO), 2018<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.prweb.com/releases/u_s_scientist_esther_sans_takeuchi_receives_european_inventor_award_2018_in_the_non_epo_countries_category/prweb15543261.htm|title=U.S. Scientist Esther Sans Takeuchi Receives European Inventor Award 2018 in the Non-EPO Countries Category|work=PRWeb|access-date=2018-11-18}}</ref>
*[https://web.archive.org/web/20130204014635/http://commcgi.cc.stonybrook.edu/am2/publish/General_University_News_2/Esther_Takeuchi_Selected_to_Receive_2013_E_V_Murphree_Award.shtml E.V. Murphree Award in Industrial & Engineering Chemistry], American Chemical Society, 2013
* Elected, [[National Academy of Engineering]], 2004<ref>{{cite news |title=Professor Esther S. Takeuchi |url=https://www.nae.edu/30841/Professor-Esther-S-Takeuchi |access-date=October 15, 2021 |publisher=National Academy of Engineering}}</ref>
* Fellow, [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]], 1999<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/COF-0978/|title=Esther Takeuchi, Ph.D. COF-0978 – AIMBE|website=aimbe.org|access-date=2018-11-18}}</ref>
* [[National Medal of Technology and Innovation]], 2008 – for inventing the [[silver vanadium oxide battery]] that powers implantable [[cardiac defibrillator]]s<ref>[http://open.nysenate.gov/legislation/bill/K1002-2009 "Honoring Esther Sans Takeuchi Upon the Occasion of Receiving the National Medal of Technology and Innovation"], New York Senate Resolution K1002-2009, Adopted Feb. 22, 2010.</ref>
* Inductee, [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]], 2011<ref name="bnl news">{{cite web|title=Energy Innovator Esther Takeuchi Elected Fellow of Electrochemical Society|url=http://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=11468 |access-date= }}</ref>
*Fellow, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], 2021<ref>{{cite news |title=Esther Takeuchi Elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=118848 |access-date=October 15, 2021 |publisher=Brookhaven National Laboratory |date=May 4, 2021}}</ref>
*[[NAS Award in Chemical Sciences]] (2022)
